Robot Doctor Servos

Servo jitters, buzzes, or twitches

Shakes, hums, or randomly moves. Below are the 5 most common causes on FTC robots, ordered from most to least likely, with how to check and fix each one.

Skip the guesswork — run the interactive diagnosisAbout 6 quick questions narrow this list down to your robot's actual problem.

Quick checks first

  • Does it buzz or jitter only at one end of its travel? Move it to each end position and listen.
  • Does the position you send keep changing even when nobody touches the controls? Print the value you pass to setPosition every loop.
  • Are several busy servos sharing neighboring ports (0–1, 2–3, 4–5) on the same hub? Count which ports your strong or heavily loaded servos use.
  • Does the servo get warm even when the mechanism isn't moving? Carefully touch the servo case after a minute of holding.
  • Does a known-good servo work in the same spot? Swap in a spare servo without changing anything else.
  • Does it still happen with a freshly charged battery? Swap to a battery straight off the charger and repeat the exact same thing.

Common causes and how to fix them

1 Servo pushing against a hard stop

If the commanded position is past where the mechanism physically stops, the servo strains, buzzes, gets hot, and draws lots of current.

How to fix it 10 min

  1. Command the position slowly in small steps and find where the mechanism actually stops. Keep the endpoints just short of it.
  2. Re-index the horn or linkage so the full range fits the mechanism.

Sources: GM0 · Servo usage tips

2 Servo ports are overloaded

Hub servo ports share power in pairs (0–1, 2–3, 4–5) at about 2 A per pair and 5 A total. Strong servos under load brown out their neighbors.

How to fix it 15 min

  1. Spread servos out: FIRST recommends using only the odd or only the even ports, so each servo gets its own pair (up to 3 per hub).
  2. Put heavily loaded servos on a REV Servo Hub or a goBILDA Servo Power Injector (6 V, much more current).
  3. Avoid the old REV Servo Power Module. GM0 warns it can fail and take the hub with it.

Sources: FTC Docs · Servo power best practices · GM0 · Servo usage tips

3 Code is sending changing positions

Two parts of the code setting different positions in the same loop, or a position that flips every loop, makes the servo twitch.

How to fix it 10 min

  1. Search the code for every setPosition on that servo. Keep one place that decides the position.
  2. Print the position you send each loop. If it bounces between values, fix the logic (often a button toggle without edge detection).
Toggle on press, not while held
boolean lastA = false;
boolean clawOpen = false;
// in the loop:
if (gamepad1.a && !lastA) clawOpen = !clawOpen;
lastA = gamepad1.a;
claw.setPosition(clawOpen ? 0.6 : 0.2);

Sources: GM0 · Common software issues

4 Servo gears are stripped or the servo is worn

Backdriving a powered servo or side-loading its shaft strips the internal gears.

How to fix it 10 min

  1. Swap in a known-good servo. If the problem moves with the servo, the servo is the problem.
  2. Do not force a powered servo by hand.
  3. Support the output with a ServoBlock or bearing, and drive mechanisms through a linkage instead of hanging them right on the spline.

Sources: GM0 · Servo usage tips

5 Battery is low or worn out

A tired battery sags under load, so motors slow down and the hub can brown out.

How to fix it 2 min

  1. Swap in a freshly charged battery and test again. That alone answers the question.
  2. Watch the voltage on the Driver Station while you drive hard. Healthy packs dip, but sitting around 9 V or lower under load is a problem.
  3. Charge at the rate the battery maker recommends (REV slim: 1.8 A on the REV charger; TETRIX: 0.9 A).
  4. Label every battery with your team number, the year, and a name, and tally charge cycles. NiMH packs get weak after roughly 200–300 cycles.
  5. Retire packs that drop fast even when full. A battery tester (like a Battery Beak) shows internal resistance.

Sources: FTC Docs · Battery care, charging, fuses · REV · Control Hub troubleshooting · REV · 12V battery troubleshooting
